description: Start here. In one call: the active vault and every registered vault, the active vault's note and link counts and health score, the markdown dialect it uses, and the tools grouped by task. If no vault is active, it says how to add one.
name: get_vault_context
title: Get Vault Context

description: Read a note's markdown, whole or in part. A whole read also returns its `hash`, which write_note, edit_note and the other write tools take as expected_hash so a change made since is not overwritten. Use at most one selector (head_lines, tail_lines, or the section ones); a partial read returns no hash.

head_lines.description: Return only the first this many lines.

heading_equals.description: Return the section under the heading with exactly this text, without its `#` markers, such as `Next steps`. Case-sensitive.

heading_level.description: Return sections that start at headings of this level, 1 to 6. Combine with heading_equals or last_sections to narrow them.

last_sections.description: Return only the last this many of the selected sections, such as the latest entries of a log.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

tail_lines.description: Return only the last this many lines.

name: read_note
title: Read Note

description: Create a note, replace one, or add text to its start or end. Replacing an existing note needs its expected_hash from read_note, so a change made since isn't lost; creating needs none. For small changes inside a note, edit_note is safer. On a Git-backed vault the write is one commit.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the path.

content.description: The markdown to write, frontmatter included if the note has any.

expected_hash.description: The note's `hash` from your last read_note. Required to overwrite an existing note, and the write is refused if the note changed since. `blind` overwrites without checking; `absent` insists the note doesn't exist yet.

mode.description: `overwrite` (default) writes the whole note; `append` and `prepend` add the content at the end or start of an existing note.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`. Missing folders are created.

name: write_note
title: Write Note

description: Change parts of a note with SEARCH/REPLACE blocks, leaving the rest as it is. Safer than write_note for small changes, since only the matched text changes. Each SEARCH text must match once in the note; close matches (whitespace, indentation) are accepted and reported as warnings.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the path.

dry_run.description: Report what the edit would change without writing it. Default false.

edits.description: One or more blocks of the form `<<<<<<< SEARCH`, the exact text to find, `=======`, the text to put instead, `>>>>>>> REPLACE`, each marker on its own line. To edit text containing a `=======` line, make all three markers 8 or more characters long.

expected_hash.description: The note's `hash` from your last read_note; the edit is refused if the note changed since. Omit to edit whatever is there now.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

name: edit_note
title: Edit Note

description: Delete a note. On a Git-backed vault it refuses when other notes link to it, unless on_backlinks is `rewrite-stale-callout` (strike those links through in the same commit) or force is true (leave them broken). On a plain-folder vault force defaults to true. get_backlinks shows what links to it.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the path.

confirm_path.description: The same path again, to confirm the deletion.

expected_hash.description: The note's `hash` from your last read_note; the delete is refused if the note changed since. Omit to delete whatever is there now.

force.description: Delete even when other notes link to it, leaving their links broken. Default false on a Git-backed vault, true on a plain-folder vault.

on_backlinks.description: `rewrite-stale-callout` to strike through the links to it in other notes, as part of the same delete.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `drafts/Old.md`.

name: delete_note
title: Delete Note

description: Move or rename a note. Git-backed vaults update inbound links (wikilinks and Markdown links) atomically by default; set update_backlinks=false for a rename-only operation. A note already at the destination is never replaced unless dest_expected_hash says so. For attachments and other files, use move_file.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the paths.

dest_expected_hash.description: What must be at the destination. Default `absent`, so an existing note is never replaced; a note's `hash` allows replacing that exact version, and `blind` replaces anything.

expected_hash.description: The note's `hash` from your last read_note; the move is refused if it changed since. Omit to move whatever is there now.

from.description: Vault-relative path of the note to move, including the extension, such as `inbox/Plan.md`.

to.description: Vault-relative path to move it to, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`. Missing folders are created.

update_backlinks.description: Rewrite links to the note in other notes so they follow it. Default true on a Git-backed vault, false on a plain-folder vault.

name: move_note
title: Move Note

description: List the notes that link to a note (its backlinks), as vault-relative paths. Use before renaming or deleting a note to see what depends on it; get_forward_links gives the other direction.

limit.description: Most backlinks to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many backlinks to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

name: get_backlinks
title: Get Backlinks

description: List the notes a note links to (its outgoing links that resolve to notes), as vault-relative paths. Broken links are not included; get_broken_links lists those.

limit.description: Most links to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many links to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

name: get_forward_links
title: Get Forward Links

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

max_hops.description: How many link hops to follow. Default 2, maximum 5; each hop can multiply the result.

offset.description: How many notes to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note to start from, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

name: get_related_notes
title: Get Related Notes

offset.description: How many top hubs to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

top_n.description: How many hubs to return. Default 10, maximum 500.

name: get_hub_notes
title: Get Hub Notes

description: List notes that other notes link to but that link to nothing themselves. These are often unfinished notes or final topics that could point onward.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many notes to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

name: get_dead_end_notes
title: Get Dead-End Notes

description: List groups of notes that link among themselves but have no link to the rest of the vault. Each item is an array of paths. They often mark separate projects or content that was never connected.

limit.description: Most clusters to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many clusters to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

name: get_isolated_clusters
title: Get Isolated Clusters

description: Score the vault's link health from 0 to 100, with counts of notes, links, broken links and orphans. Fast; use it first, then full_health_analysis or get_broken_links for detail.
name: quick_health_check
title: Quick Health Check

description: Full link-health report: the quick check's counts plus dead-end and hub counts. Slower than quick_health_check on a large vault; the lists themselves come from get_broken_links, get_dead_end_notes and get_hub_notes.
name: full_health_analysis
title: Full Health Analysis

description: List links that point to notes that don't exist: the linking note, the target as written, its line, and existing notes with similar names. Fix one by editing the link or creating the missing note.

limit.description: Most broken links to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many broken links to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

name: get_broken_links
title: Get Broken Links

description: List chains of notes that link around in a circle back to where they started. Each item is an array of paths. Cycles are normal in a wiki; this is for spotting loops in hierarchies that should not have them.

limit.description: Most cycles to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many cycles to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

name: detect_cycles
title: Detect Cycles

description: One-call overview of the vault: note and link counts, health score, folders with note counts, top hubs and dead ends, and suggested next actions. Use it to orient in an unfamiliar vault; get_vault_context is lighter.

title: Explain Vault

description: Full-text keyword search across every note, ranked by relevance (BM25). Each result has the path, title, a snippet, tags and links. Use advanced_search to filter by tag, frontmatter or folder.

limit.description: Most results to return. Default 10, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many top results to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

query.description: Words to search for. Supports tantivy query syntax: `"exact phrase"`, `+required`, `-excluded`, `title:word`.

name: search
title: Search Notes

FrontmatterFilter.description: A frontmatter key-value filter for advanced search

exclude_paths.description: Leave out notes under these vault-relative folders or paths, such as `["archive/", "templates/"]`.

frontmatter_filters.description: Only notes whose frontmatter matches every filter. Each filter is `{key, value}` and matches when the value contains `value`.

limit.description: Most results to return. Default 10, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many top results to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

query.description: Words to search for, in tantivy query syntax as for search. Use `*` to match every note and filter only.

tags.description: Only notes carrying all of these tags, without `#`, such as `["project", "active"]`.

name: advanced_search
title: Advanced Search

description: Find notes whose frontmatter field contains a value, such as `status` = `draft`. For conditions, joins or aggregates over frontmatter use query_frontmatter_sql.

key.description: Frontmatter key to match, such as `status` or `type`.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 50, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many matches to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

value.description: Value to look for in that key; a note matches when its value contains this text.

name: search_by_frontmatter
title: Search by Frontmatter

description: Find notes whose content resembles a note's, ranked by similarity, with scores. Use it to suggest reading or linking; get_related_notes follows existing links instead.

limit.description: Most recommendations to return. Default 5, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many top recommendations to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note to find relatives of, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

name: recommend_related
title: Recommend Related Notes

description: Describe the frontmatter across all notes as SQL columns: each key's name, type, how many notes have it, and whether it can be empty. Call it before query_frontmatter_sql to learn what columns exist.
name: inspect_frontmatter
title: Inspect Frontmatter

description: Run a read-only SQL SELECT against a 'files' table built from all vault note frontmatter, plus 'tags' (path, tag) and 'links' (source, target, link_type, is_valid). Each note becomes a row with 'path' + all frontmatter keys as columns. Supports WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT, subqueries, and aggregations. Only SELECT runs; results stop at 1000 rows (marked truncated, with total_rows) and a query has 10 seconds

sql.description: One SQL SELECT, such as `SELECT path, status FROM files WHERE status = 'draft' ORDER BY path`. Quote frontmatter keys with spaces or dashes in double quotes.

expected_hash.description: Default `absent`, so an existing note is never replaced. Pass the existing note's `hash` from read_note to replace that version, or `blind` to replace whatever is there.

Passing backend_opts with write_backend 'direct' is an error. The server may only allow vaults inside certain folders (allowed_vault_roots).

backend_opts.description: Settings for the `git` backend: `branch`, `author` {name, email}, `merge_strategy` (`merge-commit` or `fast-forward`), `include_ignored`, `require_commit_message`.

Passing backend_opts with write_backend 'direct' is an error. The server may only allow vaults inside certain folders (allowed_vault_roots).

backend_opts.description: Settings for the `git` backend: `branch`, `author` {name, email}, `merge_strategy` (`merge-commit` or `fast-forward`), `include_ignored`, `require_commit_message`.

name.description: A short name to refer to the vault by, without spaces, at most 64 characters, such as `notes`.

name: set_active_vault
title: Set Active Vault

description: Name the active vault, the one the note, search and graph tools work on.
name: get_active_vault
title: Get Active Vault

description: Run several note operations (create, write, edit, delete, move, frontmatter and tag changes) in one call. With write_backend=git, the batch is one atomic commit: every operation applies or none do. On a plain-folder vault they apply in order, and one that fails leaves the earlier ones applied; the result says which.

oneOf.description:
Create a new note with content. Defaults to strict-create: the
substrate adds `expect_absent`, so the loser of a concurrent-create
race aborts the entire batch with `ConcurrencyError`
(turbovault-947 / 6fo §6 reconsideration domino).

`force: Some(true)` disables `expect_absent`, falling back to
upsert semantics (caller-acknowledged blind create/overwrite —
equivalent to `WriteNote { expected_hash: None }`).

force.description:
Disable the implicit `expect_absent` precondition. Default
false; pass true to acknowledge a blind create/overwrite.

oneOf.description:
Write/overwrite a note. `expected_hash` (git blob OID hex on git
backend, SHA-256 on direct) carries an `expect_blob` precondition;
the whole batch aborts if the target file no longer matches the
expected pre-image (turbovault-c0e).

expected_hash.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency precondition checked before any operation in the batch is applied.

oneOf.description:
Delete a note. `expected_hash` guards the delete against a
concurrent modification of the target.

turbovault-0g4.7: on the **git backend**, `on_backlinks` controls inbound
wikilinks (parity with the standalone `delete_note`):
- `"refuse"` (default) — abort the batch if the note has inbound
  backlinks (prevents silently shipping broken links);
- `"rewrite-stale-callout"` — atomically `~~[[strikethrough]]~~` every
  linker in the same commit;
- `"force"` — delete and leave inbound links dangling (the pre-0g4.7
  behavior).

The direct backend ignores this field and always does a bare delete (no
atomic multi-file primitive).

expected_hash.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency precondition on the deleted file.

oneOf.description:
Move/rename a note. `expected_hash` guards the SOURCE against concurrent
modification; `dest_expected_hash` guards the DESTINATION. Both are
sentinel-or-oid strings (`<oid> | "absent" | "exists" | "blind"`), the
same shape every other batch op's `expected_hash` uses. `dest_expected_hash`
omitted = `"absent"` (the default clobber guard — refuse if the dest
exists), preserving the pre-qae.6.4 behavior. (turbovault-qae.6.4)

turbovault-0g4.6: on the **git backend**, `update_backlinks` (default
true) atomically rewrites every inbound wikilink — `[[from]]`,
`[[from|alias]]`, `[[from#section]]`, `[[from#^block]]`, `![[from]]` and
path-prefix forms — to the new target in the SAME commit, with per-source
`expect_blob` preconditions. Set it false for a rename-only move (inbound
links dangle — the pre-0g4.6 behavior). The direct backend ignores this
field and is always rename-only (it has no atomic multi-file primitive).

dest_expected_hash.description:
Optional optimistic-concurrency precondition on the destination
(sentinel-or-oid string). Omitted = `"absent"` (clobber guard).

expected_hash.description:
Optional optimistic-concurrency precondition on the source file
(sentinel-or-oid string).

oneOf.description:
Update links in a note (find and replace link target).
`expected_hash` guards the source file from concurrent
modification — important when several batch ops update siblings
of the same renamed page.

turbovault-0g4.1: apply SEARCH/REPLACE blocks to an existing note as
part of the atomic batch commit (the batch equivalent of `edit_note`).
`edits` uses the same block grammar as the tool; multiple blocks edit
multiple locations in the one file. `expected_hash` (git blob OID hex)
carries an `expect_blob` precondition — a stale pre-image aborts the
whole batch. **Git backend only**; the direct executor refuses it.

turbovault-0g4.2: set/merge frontmatter keys on a note as part of the
atomic batch commit (the batch equivalent of `update_frontmatter`).
`merge` defaults to true (deep-merge into existing frontmatter); false
replaces the frontmatter wholesale. `expected_hash` (git blob OID hex)
carries an `expect_blob` precondition. **Git backend only**.

turbovault-0g4.3: add or remove frontmatter tags on a note as part of
the atomic batch commit (the batch equivalent of `manage_tags`
add/remove). `operation` is `"add"` or `"remove"`; `"list"` is
read-only and not a batch op (rejected). `expected_hash` carries an
`expect_blob` precondition. **Git backend only**.

turbovault-0g4.4: render a template and create a note as part of the
atomic batch commit (the batch equivalent of `create_from_template`).
`force` (default false) → strict create (`expect_absent`, aborts if the
path exists); true → blind upsert. **Git backend only**.

commit_message.description: Commit message for the batch on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the operations.

operations.description: The operations, in order. Each is an object with `type` (`CreateNote`, `WriteNote`, `EditNote`, `DeleteNote`, `MoveNote`, `UpdateLinks`, `UpdateFrontmatter`, `ManageTags` or `CreateFromTemplate`) and that operation's fields, which mirror the single-note tools.

name: batch_execute
title: Batch Execute

description: Open a private Git worktree of the active vault, registered as its own vault, so a long piece of work can be written there without touching the vault until commit_fanout merges it back (or abandon_fanout drops it). Switch to it with set_active_vault. Git-backed vaults only; for a few files at once, batch_execute is simpler.

merge_strategy.description: Checked now, but the merge uses the merge_strategy given to commit_fanout: `merge-commit` or `fast-forward`.

name: begin_fanout
title: Begin Fanout

description: Merge the active fanout's work back into its base vault, then remove the worktree and unregister it. The worktree is removed even if the merge fails. Works from the base vault or the fanout itself.

commit_message.description: Message for the merge commit. A message naming the fanout is used when omitted.

merge_strategy.description: `merge-commit` records a merge commit; `fast-forward` moves the base branch to the fanout's tip and fails if the base moved meanwhile. Default the vault's git.merge_strategy, else `merge-commit`.

name: commit_fanout
title: Commit Fanout

description: Throw away the active fanout: remove its worktree and everything written there, leaving the base vault unchanged. Does nothing if no fanout is active.
name: abandon_fanout
title: Abandon Fanout

description: List fanout worktrees left behind by a server session that ended before committing or abandoning them.

vault.description: Only this vault's orphans, by name. Omit to check every Git-backed vault.

name: list_orphan_fanouts
title: List Orphan Fanouts

description: The vault's link-health report (score, counts, broken links, orphans) as one JSON or CSV document in `content`, to save or hand to another tool. To act on the findings, the get_* graph tools return them as data.
name: export_health_report
title: Export Health Report

description: Every broken link in the vault as one JSON or CSV document in `content`, to save or share. get_broken_links returns them page by page as data.
name: export_broken_links
title: Export Broken Links

description: Vault statistics (note, link, orphan and word counts, and averages per note) as one JSON or CSV document in `content`, to save or share.
name: export_vault_stats
title: Export Vault Statistics

description: A combined analysis report (health, statistics, links and clusters) as one JSON or CSV document in `content`. The largest export; use it for a full snapshot to save.
name: export_analysis_report
title: Export Analysis Report

description: Find notes whose frontmatter matches one simple condition, with each match's frontmatter. For several conditions, joins or sorting use query_frontmatter_sql.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many matches to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

name: query_metadata
title: Query Metadata

description: Read one frontmatter value from a note. Use read_note to see all of a note's frontmatter.

file.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

key.description: The frontmatter key. Use dots for nested keys, such as `author.name`.

name: get_metadata_value
title: Get Metadata Value

description: Change a note's YAML frontmatter and leave its body untouched. By default the given keys are merged into the existing frontmatter; set merge to false to replace it entirely. For tags, manage_tags adds or removes single tags.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the path.

expected_hash.description: The note's `hash` from your last read_note; the change is refused if the note changed since. Omit to change whatever is there now.

merge.description: True (default) to merge these keys into the existing frontmatter; false to replace the whole frontmatter with them.

name: update_frontmatter
title: Update Frontmatter

commit_message.description: Commit message for an add or remove on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived.

expected_hash.description: The note's `hash` from your last read_note; an add or remove is refused if the note changed since. Omit to change whatever is there now.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

tags.description: Tags to add or remove, without `#`, such as `["work", "project/alpha"]`. Not used by `list`.

name: manage_tags
title: Manage Tags

description: Check several notes at once without reading them: whether each exists, its size, when it was modified and whether it has frontmatter.

paths.description: Vault-relative paths of the notes, including extensions, such as `["projects/Plan.md", "Inbox.md"]`.

name: get_notes_info
title: Get Notes Info

description: Move or rename any file in the vault, such as an image or PDF, byte for byte. Links to it are not updated; to move a note and update the links to it, use move_note. A file already at the destination is replaced.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the paths.

confirm_from.description: The same path as `from`, repeated to confirm the move.

confirm_to.description: The same path as `to`, repeated to confirm the move.

expected_hash.description: The file's hash from your last read; the move is refused if it changed since. Omit to move whatever is there now.

from.description: Vault-relative path of the file to move, including the extension, such as `attachments/photo.png`.

to.description: Vault-relative path to move it to, including the extension.

name: move_file
title: Move File

description: Suggest notes that a note could link to, ranked by how many other notes link to both, each with its reasons. Use it when filling in a note's connections; recommend_related matches on content instead.

file.description: Vault-relative path of the note to suggest links for, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

limit.description: Most suggestions to return. Default 5, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many top suggestions to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000.

name: suggest_links
title: Suggest Links

description: Score how strongly two notes are connected, from 0.0 to 1.0, from links between them in each direction and notes that link to both, with the counts behind it and a plain-language reading.

source.description: Vault-relative path of the first note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

target.description: Vault-relative path of the second note, including the extension.

name: get_link_strength
title: Get Link Strength

description: Rank notes by how central they are in the link graph, most central first, with betweenness, closeness and eigenvector-style scores and a label such as `Central hub`. Returns the top 50 unless asked for more; get_hub_notes is a simpler ranking by link count.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many top-ranked notes to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

name: get_centrality_ranking
title: Get Centrality Ranking

description: The full guide to Obsidian Flavored Markdown as TurboVault reads it: links, embeds, callouts, frontmatter, tags and conventions, with what each is for. Long; get_ofm_quick_ref is the short version. The same text is the resource obsidian://syntax/complete-guide.
name: get_ofm_syntax_guide
title: OFM Syntax Guide

description: A one-page cheat sheet of Obsidian Flavored Markdown syntax: wikilinks, formatting, tasks, callouts, tables, embeds, frontmatter and block references. Read it before writing notes. The same text is the resource obsidian://syntax/quick-ref.
name: get_ofm_quick_ref
title: OFM Quick Reference

description: An example note that uses every Obsidian Flavored Markdown feature, to copy patterns from. The same text is the resource obsidian://examples/sample-note.
name: get_ofm_examples
title: OFM Example Note

description: Diff two notes: a unified diff, line and word changes, and a similarity score. Use compare_notes for a similarity verdict without the diff.

left.description: Vault-relative path of the first note, including the extension, such as `drafts/Plan.md`.

right.description: Vault-relative path of the second note, including the extension.

name: diff_notes
title: Diff Notes

description: Diff a note's current content against how it was before an operation in the audit trail. Find the operation_id with audit_log. Not available on Git-backed vaults, whose history is in Git.

operation_id.description: The `id` of an audit_log entry that changed this note.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

name: diff_note_version
title: Diff Note Version

description: Score one note's quality from 0 to 100 on readability, structure, completeness and staleness, plus a weighted overall score and suggestions to improve it.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

name: evaluate_note_quality
title: Evaluate Note Quality

description: Score every note's quality and summarize: average and distribution, per-dimension averages, the lowest- and highest-scoring notes, and recommendations. Slow on a large vault; use evaluate_note_quality for one note.

bottom_n.description: How many of the lowest- and highest-scoring notes to list. Default 10, maximum 500.

name: vault_quality_report
title: Vault Quality Report

description: Extract what a judge needs to check a note for hallucination, contradiction or redundancy: the factual claims in its prose, its declared citations (a `# Citations` section), structural signals (Schema and Examples sections), and an `uncited` flag for claims with no citations. TurboVault doesn't score grounding itself.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note, including the extension, such as `concepts/Revenue.md`.

name: analyze_note_grounding
title: Analyze Note Grounding

description: List notes that make factual claims but declare no citations (no `# Citations` section), most claims first. These are the notes most worth a grounding review; analyze_note_grounding shows one note's claims.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 50, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many notes to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

name: find_ungrounded_notes
title: Find Ungrounded Notes

description: Validate the vault as an Open Knowledge Format (OKF) bundle: checks every note for OKF v0.1 conformance (parseable frontmatter with a non-empty `type`) and surfaces each concept's OKF metadata (type, title, description, resource, timestamp, citation count) plus the bundle's type vocabulary. Reports non-conformant files for use as a CI gate

subtree.description: Vault-relative folder to check, such as `concepts/`. Omit to check the whole vault.

name: okf_validate
title: Validate OKF Bundle

description: Write or refresh OKF index.md files: each indexed folder gets an index.md listing its notes (with their frontmatter descriptions) and subfolders, so a reader can navigate one level at a time. Replaces an existing index.md; an index that would not change is left alone.

commit_message.description: Commit message for every index written, on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise each index gets a derived message.

directory.description: Vault-relative folder to index, such as `concepts/`. Omit for the vault root.

dry_run.description: Report the indexes that would be written without writing them. Default false.

recursive.description: Also index every folder below it. Default false.

name: generate_index
title: Generate OKF Index

description: Add an entry to a folder's OKF log.md history (OKF spec section 7), under a `## YYYY-MM-DD` heading with the newest date first: a new date becomes the top section, an existing date gains another bullet. Creates log.md if there isn't one.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the log path.

date.description: The entry's date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Default today, in local time.

directory.description: Vault-relative folder whose log.md to append to, such as `concepts/`. Omit for the vault root.

kind.description: The entry's leading bold word, such as `Update`, `Creation` or `Deprecation`. Default `Update`.

text.description: The entry's text, one line of prose.

name: append_log_entry
title: Append OKF Log Entry

description: Write the vault's link graph as one self-contained HTML page into the vault: an interactive graph of every note, a panel showing each note's rendered text and backlinks, and filtering and search. It opens in any browser with no server; the graph and markdown libraries load from a CDN.

commit_message.description: Commit message on a Git-backed vault. Required there when the vault sets git.require_commit_message; otherwise derived from the output path.

name.description: Title shown in the page. Default the vault folder's name.

output.description: Vault-relative path to write the HTML to. Default `viz.html`; an existing file there is replaced.

name: visualize
title: Visualize Vault

description: List notes not modified for a number of days, least recently modified first, with their age. Use it to find notes due for review.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 20, maximum 500.

offset.description: How many of the stalest notes to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000.

threshold_days.description: Only notes not modified for at least this many days count as stale. Default 90.

name: find_stale_notes
title: Find Stale Notes

description: Find notes about a topic even when they don't use your exact words, ranked by TF-IDF cosine similarity to the query. Use search for exact keywords and phrases.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 10, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many top results to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words, such as `quarterly revenue forecast`.

name: semantic_search
title: Semantic Search

description: Find the notes whose content is most like a given note's, ranked by TF-IDF cosine similarity. Use find_duplicates to scan the whole vault for near copies.

limit.description: Most notes to return. Default 10, maximum 100.

offset.description: How many top results to skip, for the next page. Default 0, at most 1000.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the note to compare against, including the extension, such as `projects/Plan.md`.

name: find_similar_notes
title: Find Similar Notes

description: Scan the whole vault for pairs of notes with nearly the same content, each with its similarity score, most similar first. Slow on a large vault; compare_notes checks one pair.

limit.description: Stop after finding this many pairs. Default 20, maximum 500. The scan ends early, so it can't be paged; raise the limit to see more.

threshold.description: Lowest similarity, from 0.0 to 1.0, for a pair to count as duplicates. Default 0.8.

name: find_duplicates
title: Find Duplicates

description: Compare two notes for overlap: a similarity score, the terms they share, a short diff summary, and a recommendation such as merging them. Use diff_notes for the full line-by-line diff.

left.description: Vault-relative path of the first note, including the extension, such as `drafts/Plan.md`.

right.description: Vault-relative path of the second note, including the extension.

name: compare_notes
title: Compare Notes

description: List the changes TurboVault made to the active vault, newest first: each operation's id, type, path, time and content hashes. Use an id with diff_note_version, rollback_preview or rollback_note. Not available on Git-backed vaults, whose history is in Git.

limit.description: Most entries to return. Default 50, maximum 1000.

offset.description: How many of the newest matching entries to skip, for the next page. Default 0; use `meta.pagination.next_offset` from the previous call.

operation.description: Only operations of this type: `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MOVE` or `ROLLBACK`.

path.description: Only operations on paths containing this text, such as `projects/` or `Plan.md`.

name: audit_log
title: Audit Log

description: Show what rollback_note would do for an operation, without doing it: the diff between the note now and the content it would be restored to, and any warnings. Not available on Git-backed vaults.

operation_id.description: The `id` of the audit_log entry to undo.

name: rollback_preview
title: Preview Rollback

description: Undo one operation from the audit trail: restore the note to its content before it, or remove a note it created. Run rollback_preview first to see the change. Not available on Git-backed vaults.

operation_id.description: The `id` of the audit_log entry to undo.

name: rollback_note
title: Roll Back Note

description: Summarize the audit trail: how many operations of each type, how much snapshot storage it uses, and the time span it covers. Not available on Git-backed vaults.
name: audit_stats
title: Audit Statistics
